newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT says confused by BT Australia.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT says confused by BT Australia.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said on Wednesday it was confused by Bankers Trust (BT) Australia's comments that its bid for transport group TNT Ltd was at the lower end of valuations.

The Dutch group's friendly A$2 billion ($1.58 billion) bid for TNT was thrown into doubt earlier when fund manager BT Australia earlier revealed it had built up a 19.99 percent stake in TNT and would not commit itself to accepting the cash offer.
BT Australia's equities chief Rohan Hedley has said the A$2.45/share offer is "at the lower end of a range of valuations" which his group has made on TNT.
But a KPN spokesman said BT Australia had told its financial adviser Goldman Sachs in a meeting in Australia on Wednesday that it had not decided whether to accept the bid.
"We're a bit confused about it," he told Reuters.
Later a KPN spokesman said that its financial adviser Goldman Sachs had not met with Bankers Trust Australia in Australia earlier on Wednesday.
The spokesman retracted his earlier comment that the two parties had held a meeting. "There was no contact at all," he told Reuters.
Earlier the KPN spokesman said BT Australia, a unit of New York-based Bankers Trust New York Corp, could have accumulated its stake for "a variety of reasons", but declined to comment further.
